newsitem.title: INDIA: India Reliance starts new polyester unit.
newsitem.headline: India Reliance starts new polyester unit.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals firm Reliance Industries ltd said it commissioned its fourth 30,000 tonnes a year polyester filament yarn (PFY) unit at Hazira on the western coast.

"With the commissioning of this plant, the total PFY capacity of Reliance has increased to 210,000 tonnes per year, making Reliance the sixth largest PFY producer in the world," the company said in a statement.
"This represents an increase of 40 percent over the year-end capacity of 150,000 tonnes per year at the close of financial year 1995/96 (April-March)," it said.
Reliance had commissioned its third 30,000 tonnes a year PFY plant earlier this year.

It said a new 80,000 tonnes a year polyester staple fibre (PSF) plant would be commissioned soon, which will take the firm's total PSF capacity to 270,000 tonnes per year, representing a jump of 160 percent over the year-end capacity of 100,000 tonnes per year at the close of fiscal 1995/96.
The company said an 80,000 tonnes per year bottle grade polyethylene terephthalate (PET) plant would shortly be commissioned at the Hazira works.
"The total polyester production capacity will nearly treble to about 600,000 tonnes per year on completion of all polyester capacity additions at Hazira," the statement said.

Reliance said India's PFY demand has grown at a compounded rate of 19 percent for the last 10 years. "The strong trend is likely to continue well into the future with the demand for PFY during 1997/98 is expected to cross 575,000 tonnes," it said.
